newsitem.title: CHINA: HK hawker wins salvation after Bible-quiz flop.
newsitem.headline: HK hawker wins salvation after Bible-quiz flop.

text.p: Salvation came eventually for hawker Michael Ng who was jailed after failing a Hong Kong court's bizarre, impromptu quiz on Christian knowledge.
An appeal court ruled that Ng deserved redemption because the snap theological test he flunked had made his conviction and 10-month jail term for selling pirated obscene CD-ROMs "unsafe".

The court on Tuesday set aside the punishment imposed last February by magistrate James Lee who had accused Ng, 26, of being spiritually irresponsible in seeking to swear an oath on the Bible. He insisted Ng make a non-religious affirmation.
In an exchange resembling a comedy script, Lee asked Ng the age of Jesus Christ when he died. It was 33 but Ng did not know.
At the appeal, defence lawyer Alexander King introduced a transcript, saying it had influenced the guilty verdict on Ng.
Lee: Where was Jesus born? You really should know.

Lee: Almost, not very far (from Bethlehem). You can make it there on foot.... Never take the oath on the Bible irresponsibly again...Soon you will have ample time to learn when Jesus was born and where and when he died.
The appeal court's Justice Wally Yeung said the magistrate was "clearly in error" in convicting Ng, having given a clear impression of being influenced by the exchange.
He released Ng who walked to freedom without any further spiritually challenging questions.
